key_insight: Human–machine interactions across the AI life cycle—design, testing, deployment and use—determine real-world human control and accountability in military contexts; effective governance must target interaction points, not just algorithms or platforms.
problem_solved: Clarifies how ambiguous notions of 'human control' and responsibility emerge from interaction patterns across the AI life cycle, and identifies where governance and design interventions can restore meaningful human oversight in military systems.
method: Conceptual lifecycle analysis that maps where humans interact with AI from design through field use
Interdisciplinary policy and ethical review to identify control gaps, decision bottlenecks, and accountability challenges
Synthesis of governance recommendations linking technical design choices to oversight, auditability and command structures
impact: Helps AI/ML practitioners prioritize design and process changes (e.g., interaction points, logging, human-in/over-the-loop affordances) that enable auditable human control and meet policy expectations in defense settings.
visual_elements: AI life-cycle diagram annotated with human interaction touchpoints (design, test, deployment, mission execution)
Decision-flow chart contrasting 'in-the-loop', 'on-the-loop', and 'out-of-the-loop' scenarios with associated risks
Governance matrix mapping lifecycle stages to recommended technical and policy interventions
Icons representing stakeholders (engineer, operator, commander, regulator) showing lines of accountability
paper_title: Re-thinking human–machine interaction and the governance of AI in the military domain
